quick.summary: How to use named steps to stop writing giant nested queries.
quick.takeaway: Pull nested blocks to the top and name them.

beats.line: My query has blocks stuffed inside each other. I cannot read it. Any advice?
Think of baking a cake. You prep the ingredients before you mix them.
So I should prep my tables?
Yes. Pull out those nested blocks and put them at the top.
Give each one a name. Then your main query just combines them.
In the trade, we call these common table expressions.
Can I just say named steps?
Sure. Named steps make the logic clear.
I name the messy bits at the top, then just use the names.
Exactly. Your code reads straight down like a recipe.

quiz.question: What is the best way to improve a query with many nested subqueries?
options: Pull the nested blocks to the top and name them.
Write the entire query on a single line.
Run each block as a separate file.
Keep them nested but add empty lines between them.
quiz.explanation: Extracting blocks into named steps makes your code much easier to read and maintain.

quiz.question: Named steps force your logic to be read backwards.
quiz.explanation: Named steps allow your code to read straight down from top to bottom, like a recipe.
